## Law in force

### GDPR

**Regulation (EU) 2016/679, General Data Protection Regulation**

**Status.** In force since 25 May 2018. Data concerning health, genetic and biometric data are special categories (Art. 9): processing is banned unless an Art. 9(2) condition applies, for example explicit consent (a), health or social care (h), public health (i) or research (j). DPIA (Art. 35), data protection by design (Art. 25), security (Art. 32), child consent for information society services (Art. 8)

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-AI-01`, `CORE-AI-04`, `CORE-AI-06`, `CORE-AI-07`, `CORE-CHD-01`, `CORE-CHD-02`, `CORE-COM-01`, `CORE-COM-02`, `CORE-COM-03`, `CORE-COM-04`, `CORE-DAT-01`, `CORE-DAT-02`, `CORE-DAT-03`, `CORE-DAT-04`, `CORE-DAT-05`, `CORE-DAT-06`, `CORE-DAT-07`, `CORE-DAT-08`, `CORE-DAT-09`, `CORE-DAT-10`, `CORE-DAT-11`, `CORE-DAT-12`, `CORE-DAT-13`, `CORE-DAT-14`, `CORE-DAT-15`, `CORE-DAT-16`, `CORE-DAT-17`, `CORE-GOV-01`, `CORE-GOV-02`, `CORE-LNG-01`, `CORE-SEC-01`, `CORE-SEC-02`, `CORE-SEC-03`, `CORE-SEC-04`, `CORE-SEC-06`, `CORE-SEC-07`, `CORE-TRK-01`, `CORE-TRK-02`, `CORE-TRK-03`, `CORE-TRK-04`, `E-DAT-01`, `E-LOG-01`, `R-DAT-01`, `R-DAT-02`, `R-DAT-03`, `T-DAT-01`, `T-DAT-02`, `W-DAT-02`

### CJEU-LINDEN

**CJEU, C-21/23, Lindenapotheke, 4 Oct 2024**

**Status.** Case law (Grand Chamber). Data customers enter when ordering pharmacy-only medicines online are data concerning health under Art. 9(1) GDPR, even without a prescription, where a link can be made between the product, its use and an identifiable person; certainty is not needed. Competitors can sue under unfair competition law

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DAT-01`, `CORE-TRK-02`

**Link.** [https://curia.europa.eu/jcms/upload/docs/application/pdf/2024-10/cp240159en.pdf](https://curia.europa.eu/jcms/upload/docs/application/pdf/2024-10/cp240159en.pdf)

### DSA

**Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, Digital Services Act**

**Status.** Fully applicable since 17 Feb 2024. Online platforms may not show ads based on profiling with special categories of data such as health (Art. 26(3)) and may not use dark patterns (Art. 25)

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-11

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-COM-02`, `CORE-COM-04`, `CORE-TRK-03`

**Link.** [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj)

### EPRIV

**Directive 2002/58/EC, ePrivacy Directive, Art. 5(3)**

**Status.** In force. Storing or reading information on a user's device needs consent unless strictly necessary for the service the user asked for

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-TRK-01`

**Link.** [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj)

### CJEU-SRB

**CJEU, C-413/23 P, EDPS v Single Resolution Board, 4 Sep 2025 (EU:C:2025:645)**

**Status.** Case law. Pseudonymised data stay personal for the controller that holds the key; for a recipient with no means reasonably likely to re-identify, they may not be personal data. The controller must name such recipients when it collects the data

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-19

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DAT-11`, `R-DAT-02`

**Link.** [https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-413/23%20P](https://curia.europa.eu/juris/liste.jsf?num=C-413/23%20P)

### MDR

**Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices (MDR)**

**Status.** Applies since 26 May 2021. Software with a medical intended purpose is a medical device (Art. 2(1)); Annex VIII Rule 11 classifies software. Clinical evaluation (Art. 61), quality management and post-market surveillance (Art. 10, 83 to 86), vigilance (Art. 87). Transitional periods for legacy devices were extended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** pending

### AIA

**Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Artificial Intelligence Act**

**Status.** Prohibitions (Art. 5) and AI literacy (Art. 4) apply since 2 Feb 2025. GPAI rules since 2 Aug 2025. Transparency (Art. 50) from 2 Aug 2026; machine-readable marks by 2 Dec 2026 for systems already on the market. As amended by the AI Omnibus: high-risk rules for Annex III use cases from 2 Dec 2027, and for AI in products under Annex I law (medical devices and IVDs included) from 2 Aug 2028

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Notes.** Timeline as stated by the Commission's AI Act page (last updated 19 Oct 2026): https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-AI-01`, `CORE-AI-02`, `CORE-AI-05`, `CORE-AI-08`, `M-AI-01`

**Link.** [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

## Adopted, applying later

### EHDS

**Regulation (EU) 2025/327 on the European Health Data Space**

**Status.** In force 26 Mar 2025; applies in stages: general date 26 Mar 2027, further milestones 26 Mar 2029, 2031 and 2035 (check the date for each chapter). Primary use: people's access to and control over their electronic health data; exchange of patient summaries and ePrescriptions in all Member States from 2029. EHR systems must meet Annex II (interoperability and logging components). A wellness application that claims interoperability with EHR systems must meet the same requirements, inform users, carry a label (Art. 47) and be registered in the EU database (Art. 49); interoperability never means automatic sharing (Art. 48). Secondary use covers data from wellness applications too

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Notes.** Commission page and timeline: https://health.ec.europa.eu/ehealth-digital-health-and-care/european-health-data-space-regulation-ehds_en

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DAT-09`, `CORE-GOV-02`, `CORE-SEC-07`, `E-ACC-01`, `E-INT-01`, `E-INT-02`, `E-LOG-01`, `R-DAT-03`, `R-EHD-01`, `W-EHD-01`, `W-EHD-02`

**Link.** [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/327/oj)

### CRA

**Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, Cyber Resilience Act**

**Status.** Reporting obligations from 11 Sep 2026; main obligations from 11 Dec 2027. Products covered by the MDR or IVDR are outside its scope; connected wellness devices and apps with a remote data processing part are generally in scope. The EHDS amends it

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-11

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-SEC-01`, `CORE-SEC-04`, `CORE-SEC-05`, `W-SEC-01`

**Link.** [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2847/oj](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2847/oj)

### PLD

**Directive (EU) 2024/2853 on liability for defective products**

**Status.** Applies to products placed on the market from 9 Dec 2026. Software, including AI systems and apps, is a product; damage includes medically recognised psychological harm and destruction or corruption of data. Missing security updates can make a product defective

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** pending

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-SAF-01`, `CORE-SEC-05`

**Link.** [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/2853/oj](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/2853/oj)

## Proposals

### OMNIBUS-DATA

**Digital Omnibus Regulation proposal, COM(2025) 837, procedure 2025/0360(COD)**

**Status.** Proposed 19 Nov 2025. Would make the definition of personal data relative to the holder and move device-storage consent into a new GDPR Art. 88a. EDPB-EDPS Joint Opinion 2/2026 calls the definition change a red line. Watched; HDSF relies on neither change

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-19

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DAT-11`

**Link.** [https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-new-plan-for-europe-s-sustainable-prosperity-and-competitiveness/file-digital-package](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/theme-a-new-plan-for-europe-s-sustainable-prosperity-and-competitiveness/file-digital-package)

### MDR-REV

**Proposal for a targeted revision of the MDR and IVDR, COM(2025) 1023, procedure 2025/0404(COD)**

**Status.** Adopted by the Commission 16 Dec 2025. Would amend the MDR, the IVDR, Regulation (EU) 2022/123 and the AI Act, including MDR classification rules and software classification. With Parliament and Council in 2026 (Council compromise texts circulating). Watched

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-GOV-02`, `CORE-QUA-04`, `M-WCH-01`

**Link.** [https://oeil.europarl.europa.eu/oeil/en/procedure-file?reference=2025/0404(COD)](https://oeil.europarl.europa.eu/oeil/en/procedure-file?reference=2025/0404(COD))

**Status.** Adopted 8 Jul 2026 for public consultation (until 30 Oct 2026); not final. Clarifies when data can be considered anonymous and gives a framework to check whether anonymisation worked

**EDPB Guidelines 03/2022 on deceptive design patterns in social media platform interfaces: how to recognise and avoid them, version 2.0**

### MDCG-2019-11

**MDCG 2019-11 rev. 1, Guidance on qualification and classification of software in Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR)**

**Status.** Revision 1 published 17 Jun 2025. Qualification depends on the intended purpose the manufacturer claims, not on how the software works. Adds medical device artificial intelligence (MDAI), modular software, disease-prevention software under Rule 11, Annex XVI products and links to the EHDS

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-AI-03`, `CORE-QUA-01`, `CORE-QUA-02`, `CORE-QUA-03`, `CORE-QUA-04`, `M-QUA-01`, `W-QUA-01`, `W-QUA-02`

**Link.** [https://health.ec.europa.eu/latest-updates/update-mdcg-2019-11-rev1-qualification-and-classification-software-regulation-eu-2017745-and-2025-06-17_en](https://health.ec.europa.eu/latest-updates/update-mdcg-2019-11-rev1-qualification-and-classification-software-regulation-eu-2017745-and-2025-06-17_en)

### MDCG-2025-4

**MDCG 2025-4, Guidance on the safe making available of medical device software (MDSW) apps on online platforms**

**Status.** Published 16 Jun 2025. Uploading a medical device app to a platform is placing it on the market. Users should see the device information before download; platforms should keep medical device apps apart from wellness and lifestyle apps. Covers MDR, IVDR and DSA roles

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-QUA-03`, `M-APP-01`, `W-QUA-02`

**Link.** [https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-sector/new-regulations/guidance-mdcg-endorsed-documents-and-other-guidance_en](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-sector/new-regulations/guidance-mdcg-endorsed-documents-and-other-guidance_en)

### MDCG-2025-6

**MDCG 2025-6 / AIB 2025-1, FAQ on the interplay between the MDR and IVDR and the Artificial Intelligence Act**

**Status.** Published 19 Jun 2025, the first joint guidance of the MDCG and the AI Board. AI that is a medical device, or a safety component of one, and needs a notified body is a high-risk AI system under AI Act Art. 6(1); the AI Act does not change the MDR or IVDR class. An MDR user is not automatically an AI Act deployer

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-AI-03`, `M-AI-01`, `M-AI-02`

**Link.** [https://health.ec.europa.eu/latest-updates/mdcg-2025-6-faq-interplay-between-medical-devices-regulation-vitro-diagnostic-medical-devices-2025-06-19_en](https://health.ec.europa.eu/latest-updates/mdcg-2025-6-faq-interplay-between-medical-devices-regulation-vitro-diagnostic-medical-devices-2025-06-19_en)

### MDCG-2020-1

**MDCG 2020-1, Guidance on clinical evaluation (MDR) and performance evaluation (IVDR) of medical device software**

**Status.** Published March 2020. Valid clinical association, technical performance and clinical performance as the three parts of the evidence for software

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** pending

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-SAF-03`, `M-CLN-01`

**Link.** [https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-sector/new-regulations/guidance-mdcg-endorsed-documents-and-other-guidance_en](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medical-devices-sector/new-regulations/guidance-mdcg-endorsed-documents-and-other-guidance_en)

### AIA-GL-ART50

**Commission Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of AI systems (Art. 50 AI Act)**

**Status.** Published 20 Jul 2026; obligations apply from 2 Aug 2026. Chatbots, AI agents and avatars disclose from the first interaction, clearly and accessibly; the 'obvious' exception is read restrictively. Synthetic media carries machine-readable marks

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-AI-02`

**Link.** [https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/guidelines-transparency-obligations-providers-and-deployers-ai-systems](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/guidelines-transparency-obligations-providers-and-deployers-ai-systems)

**Commission Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence practices established by Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), C(2025) 884**

**Status.** Published 4 Feb 2025. Not binding; examples for Art. 5, including harmful manipulation and exploitation of vulnerability due to age, disability or a social or economic situation

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

## Research and other frameworks

### R-TANGARI2021

**Tangari G, Ikram M, Ijaz K, Kaafar MA, Berkovsky S. Mobile health and privacy: cross sectional study. BMJ 2021;373:n1248**

**Status.** Peer reviewed. 20,991 mHealth apps on Google Play; 15,838 free apps analysed in depth. 28.1% had no privacy policy, and only 47% of user data transmissions matched the policy

**Jurisdiction.** international · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-COM-01`, `CORE-TRK-01`, `CORE-TRK-04`

**Link.** [https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.n1248](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.n1248)

### R-HUCKVALE2019

**Huckvale K, Torous J, Larsen ME. Assessment of the data sharing and privacy practices of smartphone apps for depression and smoking cessation. JAMA Netw Open 2019;2(4):e192542**

**Status.** Peer reviewed. Of 36 top-ranked apps, 29 sent data to Facebook or Google services; only 12 disclosed this in a privacy policy

**Jurisdiction.** international · **Verified.** 2026-11-22

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-TRK-01`, `CORE-TRK-04`, `W-DAT-02`

**Link.** [https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2019.2542](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2019.2542)

### R-MARS2015

**Stoyanov SR, Hides L, Kavanagh DJ, Zelenko O, Tjondronegoro D, Mani M. Mobile App Rating Scale: a new tool for assessing the quality of health mobile apps. JMIR mHealth uHealth 2015;3(1):e27**

**Status.** Peer reviewed. 23-item scale with four objective subscales (engagement, functionality, aesthetics, information quality) and a subjective one; excellent internal consistency (alpha .90). A user version (uMARS) followed in 2016

**Jurisdiction.** international · **Verified.** 2026-11-23

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DES-03`, `CORE-DES-04`

**Link.** [https://doi.org/10.2196/mhealth.3422](https://doi.org/10.2196/mhealth.3422)

### R-GALESIC2009

**Galesic M, Garcia-Retamero R, Gigerenzer G. Using icon arrays to communicate medical risks: overcoming low numeracy. Health Psychology 2009;28(2):210-216**

**Status.** Peer reviewed. Icon arrays increased accuracy of understanding for people with low and high numeracy, including older adults

**Jurisdiction.** international · **Verified.** 2026-11-23

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DES-01`

**Link.** [https://pure.mpg.de/pubman/item/item_2099767_5/component/file_2562291/MG_Using_2009.pdf](https://pure.mpg.de/pubman/item/item_2099767_5/component/file_2562291/MG_Using_2009.pdf)

### R-NOUWENS2020

**Nouwens M, Liccardi I, Veale M, Karger D, Kagal L. Dark patterns after the GDPR: scraping consent pop-ups and demonstrating their influence. CHI 2020**

**Status.** Peer reviewed. Only 11.8% of consent pop-ups on 680 UK sites met minimal EU-law requirements; removing the opt-out button from the first page raised consent by 22 to 23 percentage points; granular controls on the first page lowered it by 8 to 20 points

**Jurisdiction.** international · **Verified.** 2026-11-23

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DES-02`

**Link.** [https://doi.org/10.1145/3313831.3376321](https://doi.org/10.1145/3313831.3376321)

### R-TRACTINSKY2000

**Tractinsky N, Katz AS, Ikar D. What is beautiful is usable. Interacting with Computers 2000;13(2):127-145**

**Status.** Peer reviewed. Perceived aesthetics strongly correlated with perceived usability before and after use; the system's aesthetics affected post-use perceptions of usability, while actual usability did not

**Jurisdiction.** international · **Verified.** 2026-11-23

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DES-03`

**Link.** [https://doi.org/10.1016/S0953-5438(00)00031-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0953-5438(00)00031-X)

### R-HLS-EU2015

**Sørensen K, Pelikan JM, Röthlin F et al. Health literacy in Europe: comparative results of the European health literacy survey (HLS-EU). Eur J Public Health 2015;25(6):1053-1058**

**Status.** Peer reviewed; 8,000 people in eight countries. 12% had insufficient and 47% limited health literacy, varying from 29% to 62% by country; higher among people with financial deprivation, low education or old age

**Jurisdiction.** EU · **Verified.** 2026-11-23

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-DES-01`, `CORE-DES-05`, `CORE-LNG-01`

**Link.** [https://doi.org/10.1093/eurpub/ckv043](https://doi.org/10.1093/eurpub/ckv043)

**NICE, Evidence standards framework for digital health technologies (ECD7)**

**Status.** Published Dec 2018, updated Aug 2022 (AI and adaptive algorithms, alignment with regulation). UK framework, used here as international best practice: evidence expected rises with the technology's function and risk

**Jurisdiction.** UK · **Verified.** 2026-11-23

**Rules citing it.** `CORE-SAF-05`

**Link.** [https://www.nice.org.uk/corporate/ecd7](https://www.nice.org.uk/corporate/ecd7)

## Open discussions and watch list

| Item | What to watch | Effect on HDSF |
|---|---|---|
| EHDS implementing acts | Commission implementing acts due by 26 Mar 2027: European EHR exchange format, labels for wellness applications, testing environments | Concrete technical steps for E-INT-01, E-INT-02 and W-EHD-01 |
| MDR and IVDR targeted revision | COM(2025) 1023: Parliament and Council positions, trilogue, final software classification rules | CORE-QUA-02, M-QUA-01 and M-WCH-01 may change; adopted text moves into Level 1 with its dates |
| AI Act high-risk guidance | Commission guidance and harmonised standards for high-risk AI, ahead of 2 Aug 2028 for medical devices | Detail for M-AI-01 |
| EDPB Guidelines 1/2026 on scientific research | Final text after the 2026 consultation | Confirm R-DAT-01 and R-DAT-02 |
| Digital Omnibus (data) | Changes to the definition of personal data and to device-storage consent | CORE-DAT-11 and CORE-TRK-01 might change; HDSF relies on neither change |
| EU health app quality label | Follow-up to Label2Enable and use of ISO/TS 82304-2 in national app libraries and reimbursement | CORE-SAF-02 and CORE-SAF-03 may become stronger |
| National packs | Portugal (SPMS, INFARMED, CNPD) and other Member States: national app assessment and reimbursement schemes | National notes on rules; possibly country packs as in CSEF |
